story: Change the share of class 1. A pure mixture has zero uncertainty; an even mix is hardest to predict. Gini and entropy agree about that pattern but use different scales.

aha.observation: At an even mixture, Gini is 0.5 and entropy is 1 bit. Both return to zero at either pure endpoint.

controls.label: Class 1 fraction p
controls.effect: Change the mixture, both curve markers and both computed impurity values.
Restore the declared initial inputs and the initial evidence.

data.title: Substitute the same mixture twice.
data.heading: Probe Gini and entropy together
data.prompt: how does Gini impurity change as the fraction of one class goes from 0 to 1, compared with entropy?
data.instructions: Move p from a pure endpoint to an even mix. Compare both curves at the same fraction.

reference.title: Gini impurity and entropy
reference.caption: Worked example. $G(p)=2p(1-p)$ and $H(p)=-p\log_2 p-(1-p)\log_2(1-p)$. Rounded samples. At the endpoints, the zero-share term vanishes by continuity.

calculations: At p=0 or 1, define 0*log2(0) by its zero limit; evaluate entropy as 0 without computing log2(0).
Curve samples are recomputed from these formulas; source samples round to 3 decimals. Peak scaling uses G/0.5 and H/1, not raw-score equality.
The mixture strip encodes proportions continuously; it is not an invented integer training sample.
